purpose: is the rewritten predict_full_q bit-identical to the old one, and is a larger decode chunk actually faster?
device: cpu, 6 torch threads, min of 2 repeats per configuration
caveat: timed while four training arms shared the box, so the ABSOLUTE seconds are inflated; every configuration was timed under the same contention, so the ratios are the quantity to read
what_holds: the rewritten path is BIT-IDENTICAL to the old one at both sizes, diagonal included, so the change is safe
chunk 32768 changes the answer by 6.2-6.7e-07 relative on the factor, independently reproducing the earlier 4.6e-07 claim to within a factor of 1.5
what_is_withdrawn: the 1.50x speedup attributed to this rewrite: measured 0.974x at q=711 and 1.000x at q=10812.  The reasoning offered for it was also wrong -- the old M - M.T guard was said to dominate, and it does not: 273 s is decode

the 2.08x attributed to chunk 32768: on CPU it is SLOWER, 0.845x and 0.913x, as well as lossy.  Whatever produced 2.08x was not this measurement; it may have been a GPU run, which is untested here and must not be assumed
consequence: the decode chunk rule stands on correctness alone, not on speed.  The real headroom was elsewhere: a single arm used 2.14 of the box's 16 cores with the GPU at 40 % and 3 GB of 32 GB, so four arms now run concurrently; per-step time went 0.0514 s to about 0.105 s and the GPU to 96 %, a net 1.95x, not 4x.
